title: Translation invariance of the normalized affine-space integration
statement:
Use the finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, for arbitrary $n\geq1$, and the field $k$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $d\geq0$, and put $V=\mathbf A^d_S$ with projection $q:V\to S$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Work in the ordinary etale derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of the schemes $T$ below [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with the ordinary etale Tate line and its pullback identifications [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Put $L=A_V(d)[2d]$ and let $t_q:Rq_!L\to A_S$ be the normalized trace [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], with ordinary compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

For a section $a:S\to\mathbf A^d_S$, let $\tau_a:V\to V$ be the $S$-automorphism $z\mapsto z-a$. For the Cartesian square with both vertical maps $q$, bottom map $1_S$ and top map $\tau_a$, let $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\tau_a}:Rq_!L\to Rq_!\tau_a^*L$ be the canonical compact-support exchange, normalized as in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and let $\kappa_a:\tau_a^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ be the Tate pullback identification. Then the actual derived morphisms satisfy
$$t_q\circ Rq_!(\kappa_a)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\tau_a}=t_q.$$
This equality includes the universal translation over $P=\mathbf A^d_S$, with $a$ its tautological section after base change, and commutes with every base change $S'\to S$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Under the specified Tate and compact-support comparisons [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], it is also the equality of the corresponding pro-etale integration maps. Concretely, at every annihilating prime-power level, use the trivial rank-d bundle integration `vectorIntegration` and its canonical `vectorSite` comparison; the affine-trace counit is identified with `vectorBundleIntegration` by the affine vector-integration construction [def-amb-vector-integration].

proof.text: First work on the ordinary étale site. The finite-type $k$-scheme $S$ is Noetherian, and so are $P=\mathbf A^d_S$ and $V_P=V\times_SP$; the affine polynomial charts give the needed separated finite-type maps. Let $q_P:V_P\to P$ be the base change of $q$, let $a_P:P\to V$ be the tautological section, and let $\tau_P:V_P\to V_P$ be $(z,a)\mapsto(z-a,a)$. It is an automorphism over $P$, with inverse $(z,a)\mapsto(z+a,a)$. Apply [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] to $q_P$, $\tau_P$, and the canonical pullback isomorphism $\tau_P^*L\simeq L$. This gives the actual compact-support action $\rho_P:Rq_{P!}L\to Rq_{P!}L$ and its compatibility with every base change. By the base-change clause of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], the normalized trace $t_P:Rq_{P!}L\to A_P$ is an isomorphism and is the pullback of $t_q$ along $P\to S$.

proof.text: Conjugate the universal action by the specified trace: $\alpha=t_P\circ\rho_P\circ t_P^{-1}:A_P[0]\to A_P[0]$. It is an automorphism of the constant $A_P$-module sheaf. By full faithfulness of degree-zero sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], it is induced by a unique $A_P$-linear sheaf automorphism $\alpha_0$. Module linearity makes $\alpha_0$ multiplication by $b=\alpha_0(1)$, and the inverse action shows that $b$ is a unit. The section $b$ is a Zariski-locally constant function with values in $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant]. Pullback of $b$ along any base-change section is the scalar by which the corresponding translated trace is multiplied, by the action and trace base-change equations in the two cited lemmas.

source.place: Step 1: translation, sentence 4 ('identified with the constant sheaf by integration, is multiplication by a section of the locally constant sheaf of units of $\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ on $V$')

proof.text: For every geometric point $\bar s\to S$, the fibre $P_{\bar s}=\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ is nonempty and connected: its coordinate ring is a nonzero domain (and for $d=0$ it is the one-point scheme). The restriction of $b$ to this fibre is locally constant, and its value at the origin is $1$, because the universal translation restricted along the zero section is the identity and [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] gives $\rho_{1,1}=1$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-connected-locally-constant-map] makes $b|_{P_{\bar s}}=1$. Every point of $P$ lies in such a geometric fibre, so the section/function identification of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant] gives $b=1$ globally. Therefore $\alpha=1$ and $t_P\circ\rho_P=t_P$.

proof.text:
Pull the universal equality back along the section $a:S\to P$. The action base-change identity of [lem-amb-compact-action-base-change] identifies the pulled-back action with $Rq_!(\kappa_a)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\tau_a}$, while the affine trace base-change identity of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] identifies the pulled-back $t_P$ with $t_q$. Thus
$$t_q\circ Rq_!(\kappa_a)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,\tau_a}=t_q.$$
In the recorded coordinate-tower model, [lem-trf-ambient-affine-translation-trace] supplies precisely this ordinary equation for ambientAffineTranslationExchange followed by ambientAffineTranslationTate and the normalized affineTraceCounit; apply it both on $S$ at $a$ and on the parameter scheme $P$ at its tautological coordinates. The same argument after any $S'\to S$ gives the asserted universal and arbitrary-base-change compatibility. Finally [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] carries this actual ordinary étale equality, with the specified Tate and compact-support comparisons, to the corresponding pro-étale integration maps.

split_report.summary: Split the universal translation argument into four steps. I checked the finite-coefficient ordinary étale construction, the universal translation action and its base-change coherence, the scalar multiplier on the affine-space trace, connected geometric fibres forcing that scalar to be one, and the pullback to an arbitrary section. The final comparison uses the existing vector-integration site comparison. No new nodes were needed; the existing linear trace-invariance lemma is a distinct linear-change statement and is not a duplicate.

tool_uses.why: Generic compact-support automorphism action and its arbitrary-base-change coherence; the smooth-purity unit only uses this action as an input.
Generic normalized affine-space counit trace, its invertibility, and its base-change formula; the translation argument does not construct the affine trace.
Generic identification of derived maps between degree-zero constant sheaves with sheaf maps, used to express the conjugated action as multiplication.
Generic description of sections of a constant sheaf as locally constant functions, used for the scalar multiplier.
Generic fact that a locally constant function on a connected fibre is constant.
Generic Noetherianity of the affine-space bases and their compactifications needed for the finite-coefficient action and exchange lemmas.
